topic:
Honest adaptation for the full vector of attributable direct and spillover effects in a sparse Gaussian factor panel. Fix known N,r,s with 1<=r<N, 1<=s, 2s+r<=N, and feasible fixed positive bounds A,B,K,d_lower,d_upper,delta_d,sigma_lower,sigma_upper. Observe every unit in T0 untreated pre periods and T1 treated post periods. Potential outcomes obey Y_t(0)=Lambda f_t+epsilon_t before the break and Y_u(0)=Lambda g_u+epsilon_u, Y_u(1)=Y_u(0)+beta after the break, with mutually independent homoskedastic Gaussian errors of unknown bounded scale. Lambda=UD, U orthonormal and unknown, D has bounded positive distinct singular strengths separated by delta_d. Pre factors are unknown deterministic arrays with exact zero mean, covariance I and norm bounded by K. Post factors have mean a, centered covariance at most I and bounded centered norm, with ||Lambda a||<=A; no post covariance lower bound is imposed, so constant post factors are included. beta is s-sparse in [-B,B]^N with unknown support and no minimum nonzero effect. Allow arbitrary diverging T0,T1. Derive all subspace estimation and concentration from these primitives, allowing all procedures full-panel access. This is a stated Gaussian subclass of the He-Li-Shi-Miao fixed-factor causal model, not their entire error class.

Let L=col(U), kappa_s(L)=min_{|S|=2s} sigma_min((I-UUprime)E_S), equivalently min_{|C|=N-2s} sigma_min(U_C). M(0) includes kappa=0; M(gamma) restricts kappa>=gamma and only nonempty strata are considered. A measurable compact confidence set C(Y) subset [-B,B]^N is globally honest if its finite-sample coverage of the whole labeled beta vector is at least .95 uniformly over M(0). At each sample-size pair define R_ad(gamma) as the infimum of worst-case expected Euclidean diameter on M(gamma) over globally honest procedures; define R_or analogously with honesty only over M(gamma), allowing gamma as an input but not U or support. Empty/singleton sets have diameter zero. Characterize both frontiers up to fixed-class constants over every nonempty gamma stratum, derive their adaptation ratio, and construct one gamma-agnostic globally honest confidence set attaining the adaptive frontier simultaneously. The exact piecewise rates and any adaptation penalty are answer-open. Require explicit finite computation via support enumeration and joint Gaussian mean/subspace inversion, same-class lower bounds using original full observations, and bounded-signal saturation. The sparse uniqueness iff is a supporting lemma, not the paper. A conservative inverse-kappa bound alone, a beta-min support-selection theorem, or an assumed subspace rate does not discharge the kernel.

Checked mechanism: N=8,r=2,s=3, L spanned by rows (1,i), i=1,...,8, has orthonormal kappa_3=.06586041095768687, beyond the anchor count condition permitting only two affected units. Within the same s=3 class, U=[e1,(e2+...+e8)/sqrt7] and (m,beta)=(0,.25e1) or (.5e1,-.25e1) give identical observations with constant post factors; scale to fit smaller fixed positive bounds. Repeated pre factors +/-sqrt2 e1 and +/-sqrt2 e2 verify exact normalization. Consumers are He et al.'s Jordan-conflict/Beijing-pollution analyses and mlsynth RRSC's per-unit interference intervals. Compare explicitly against He et al. arXiv:2411.01249v2 and Wei arXiv:2608.13466; Wei already supplies donor-classification-free partial-ID inference in a different envelope model. Generic cospark and sparse-error stability are prior art. Novelty must be the derived sharp honest-inference/adaptation frontier with estimated loading geometry.

PRESOLVE EVIDENCE REQUIRING VERIFICATION: An exact Gaussian pre-panel covariance second moment yields a finite-sample loading-space region. Projecting two accepted sparse decompositions onto the true loading complement gives an expected-diameter bound without a logarithmic failure-event remainder. Compensated loading rotations with constant post factors give lower bounds from the original observations. The derived oracle and globally honest rates coincide throughout gamma<=kappa_star/2; no weak-boundary adaptation penalty is established. In the admissible N=3,r=s=1 case, maximal margin leaves four loading lines. The oracle near-endpoint contribution is A min(T0^(-1/2),1-3gamma^2), whereas global honesty retains the pre-panel cost. Zero margin, small effects, saturation, unequal sample sizes, and generic-reduction checks were examined. These derivations are unverified and the manuscript's compressed steps remain obligations.
UNRESOLVED BOTTLENECK: Prove the general same-sample oracle characterization across every nonempty margin stratum, including disconnected near-maximal geometries and finite component-classification transitions. A modulus sandwich with different resolution constants is insufficient.
EARLY KILL TEST: On N=8,r=2,s=3, evaluate the sparse-compatible two-subspace optimization near certified maximal-margin geometries and test a concrete component rule against original Gaussian laws. Pivot or stop if bounded analytic follow-up cannot produce a nontrivial matching characterization, or established theory already supplies it.
STRONGEST-FORM DRAFT (unverified, gaps listed inside): <repo-root>/internal/presolve_drafts/panel_interference_decoding_adaptation.md.

open_problems.open_problem: Determine the sharp finite-sample globally honest and margin-oracle expected Euclidean-diameter frontiers for the full sparse effect vector over every nonempty loading-margin stratum, including whether a single margin-agnostic procedure incurs a weak-boundary adaptation penalty.

source_refs.claim: The fixed-N method uses a majority-valid-controls condition, asymptotic selection, and entrywise bootstrap intervals; uncertainty from selecting valid controls remains difficult to quantify.
source_refs.author: Peiyu He, Yilin Li, Xu Shi, and Wang Miao

source_refs.claim: Honest adaptation for a full sparse regression vector has a testing-driven boundary and may require separation even under regular observed designs.
source_refs.author: Richard Nickl and Sara van de Geer

source_refs.excerpt: The exact continuum minimax frontier and sharp simultaneous excess remain unproved
Promote the continuum inversion handle into a finite discretization theorem with nested acceptance regions
Develop the weak-gap handle into a proved two-path lower bound and a matching stabilized-band construction

open_problems.why_unsolved: He et al. obtain selection-based asymptotic inference under a count restriction stronger than sparse uniqueness, not globally honest confidence sets for the labeled vector down to zero effects. Classical sparse-confidence-set theory treats an observed design, whereas here the inverse operator is an unknown loading subspace estimated from the same pre-panel and its restricted margin can vanish without an ordinary spectral collision. Prior CausalSmith work obtained only finite-grid duality or constant-factor continuum results: exact coverage transfer, continuum decision duality, measurable attainment, and same-class compensated-rotation lower bounds remain missing. Constant post factors eliminate post-period information about the geometry, so an assumed subspace rate or a conservative inverse-margin bound cannot determine the frontier or adaptation ratio.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A resolution would give matching piecewise upper and lower formulas for R_ad(gamma) and R_or(gamma), including unequal-sample and bounded-signal saturation regimes, plus a proved finite support-enumeration and joint Gaussian mean/subspace inversion whose margin-free confidence set has uniform 0.95 coverage and simultaneously attains the adaptive frontier.

writing_exemplar.why: Its motivation moves directly from contaminated synthetic-control donors to sparse attributable effects and the applications requiring vector uncertainty.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Synthetic controls rely on unaffected donors -> interference contaminates an unknown subset -> factor adjustment turns effects into sparse outliers -> honest joint uncertainty for the full labeled vector remains unresolved

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt the reduction of honest adaptive diameter to composite testing, including mixture lower bounds and confidence-set constructions that do not condition on correct support recovery.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Both problems seek Euclidean confidence sets for a sparse vector with honesty over a larger union model, but the causal-panel inverse operator is estimated and its restricted singular margin is the adaptation index.

method_exemplars.technique: Carry over nonasymptotic spectral-projector uncertainty and Gaussian comparison, replacing i.i.d. covariance linearization by the deterministic-factor Gaussian pre-panel second moment before joint sparse-mean inversion.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The nuisance governing causal inversion is a loading-space projector, so a valid effect set must propagate its finite-sample uncertainty.

method_exemplars.technique: Use between-class ordered moduli to compare subclass-oracle precision with union-wide honest precision and to construct bias-aware adaptive procedures.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The desired adaptation ratio is a geometric subclass-versus-union confidence-set problem indexed by the sparse-inversion margin.

open_problems.open_problem: Solve the same-sample oracle expected-diameter problem near maximal sparse-uniqueness margins when the feasible loading-space stratum has disconnected components, including the exact sample-size transitions at which component classification becomes possible.

source_refs.excerpt: the genuinely noisy sqrt(n)-scaled local experiment, but it needs a new proposal
exhibit a complete J=3 worked Gaussian donor-face program with a computed least-favorable prior
The explicit Gaussian maximum benchmark fails the early optimality test.

open_problems.why_unsolved: The prior donor-face run showed that a simultaneous Gaussian-maximum hull can be strictly suboptimal and that replacing noisy effect coordinates by noiseless component labels invalidates transfer to the original observations. Sparse factor decoding has a harder composite geometry because component membership is jointly induced by support incidence and loading orientation, while the pre-panel used for classification is also used to build the effect set. Pairwise modulus bounds with different resolution constants do not characterize collective confusion among components, and conditioning on a correctly classified component suppresses precisely the same-sample uncertainty the oracle frontier must retain.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A resolution would provide an exact or constant-matched finite Gaussian decision characterization for every disconnected near-maximal margin geometry, an explicit component-aware confidence-set rule, and matching lower and upper bounds under the original joint Gaussian observations that identify each finite component-classification transition.

writing_exemplar.why: It organizes inference around honest precision on geometrically different subclasses rather than model-selection consistency.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: A union model contains easier separated subclasses -> oracle precision depends on subclass geometry -> noisy classification couples coverage across subclasses -> characterize the component-specific decision frontier

method_exemplars.technique: Derive confidence-set risk from a constrained Gaussian testing dual with least-favorable priors and finite-action purification.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Each finite collection of sparse-compatible loading components induces a restricted-location Gaussian decision problem.

method_exemplars.technique: Average alternatives over discrete support labels and control mixture affinity rather than maximizing pairwise distances.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Loading components can be collectively indistinguishable even when individual component pairs appear separable.

open_problems.open_problem: Extend donor-classification-free envelope identification from a scalar treated-unit effect to the simultaneous labeled vector of direct and spillover effects, deriving a sharp identified set and joint inference when all coordinates share estimated covariance inputs.

source_refs.claim: Wei notes that simultaneous vector targets require new spillover definitions, restrictions, and covariance inputs and are not developed in the scalar analysis.
source_refs.author: Shengbin Wei

source_refs.claim: Bootstrap tests of solvability for estimated equality and inequality systems cover partially identified models but are not specialized to a simultaneous panel-interference vector.
source_refs.author: Leonard Goff and Eric Mbakop

source_refs.claim: The paper develops estimation and confidence regions for set-identified parameters defined through econometric criterion functions and moment restrictions.
source_refs.author: Victor Chernozhukov, Han Hong, and Elie Tamer

open_problems.why_unsolved: Wei's scalar candidate inversion exploits a fixed-dimensional finite representation, but a full labeled vector changes the admissible spillover object, introduces shared nuisance covariance across coordinates, and demands simultaneous rather than candidatewise coverage. Projecting separate scalar inversions need not be sharp because it discards cross-coordinate compatibility restrictions. The literature scan found scalar unknown-interference envelopes, point-identification results under specified spillover structure, and general estimated-system inference, but no donor-classification-free sharp vector region with joint uniform coverage.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A resolution would give an exact finite polyhedral or conic representation of the sharp identified set for the full effect vector and an implementable Gaussian or bootstrap test inversion covering that vector set uniformly with a proved joint limit law or finite-sample error bound.

writing_exemplar.why: It provides the closest motivation and separates comparison validity, substantive spillover restrictions, finite representation, and inference.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Unknown donor contamination destroys scalar point identification -> donor weights impose common relative-effect restrictions -> application restrictions yield a sharp scalar set -> policy analysis requires the unresolved simultaneous direct-and-spillover vector

method_exemplars.technique: Generalize the full-simplex reduction and Farkas-certificate argument from one candidate effect to a joint vector with shared spillover and counterfactual restrictions.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The requested vector set is the direct multivariate analogue of Wei's scalar compatibility system.

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt normalized infeasibility statistics, near-feasible recentering, and bootstrap calibration over nearly optimal dual certificates to a vector-indexed family of estimated systems.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Once vector compatibility has a finite representation, coverage reduces to uniform inference on solvability under common sampling perturbations.

method_exemplars.technique: Use criterion-level-set inference and projection arguments to distinguish coverage of an identified set from coverage of individual compatible points.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The resolution requires joint inference for a multivariate identified set, not coordinatewise candidate acceptance.

open_problems.open_problem: Under an explicitly bounded post-intervention loading-drift class, characterize the sharp partial-identification region and honest confidence-set diameter for the complete sparse effect vector rather than assuming exact loading stability.

source_refs.claim: Time-invariant loadings are assumed in the main theory; post-intervention loading perturbations are examined through simulations rather than an identification or coverage theorem.
source_refs.author: Peiyu He, Yilin Li, Xu Shi, and Wang Miao

source_refs.claim: Synthetic-control estimators can remain biased under imperfect pretreatment fit because the relevant linear projection need not be stable before and after treatment.
source_refs.author: Bruno Ferman and Cristine Pinto

source_refs.claim: Bounded departures from an exact extrapolation restriction produce partial identification and uniformly valid sensitivity inference.
source_refs.author: Ashesh Rambachan and Jonathan Roth

open_problems.why_unsolved: Loading drift adds a post-period term outside the learned pre-loading space that can be confounded with sparse direct and spillover effects, so the exact projection decomposition fails at its first step. Simulations do not establish sharpness or uniform coverage. Ferman and Pinto diagnose instability bias, while Rambachan and Roth show how bounded extrapolation violations can support sensitivity analysis, but neither derives vector bounds when a bounded loading perturbation interacts with unknown sparse effects and an estimated factor subspace.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A resolution would define a normed loading-drift class, derive a sharp optimization characterization of the identified set for beta and its diameter as functions of the drift radius and kappa_s, and construct a uniformly valid confidence region with matching minimax upper and lower diameter bounds.

writing_exemplar.why: Its motivation centers the danger of extrapolating a pre-period factor relationship into the post period when fit or stability is imperfect.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Synthetic controls extrapolate pre-period relationships -> imperfect fit or changing projections creates post-period bias -> exact loading stability is not empirically guaranteed -> bounded drift should yield explicit effect-vector sensitivity regions

method_exemplars.technique: Translate a bounded violation class into support-function bounds for the causal target and prove sharpness by constructing admissible nuisance paths attaining the endpoints.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Loading drift is an explicit violation of the pre-to-post extrapolation restriction, analogous to bounded post-treatment departures from parallel trends.

method_exemplars.technique: Encode support-enumerated sparse decompositions and bounded drift as finite feasibility systems, then invert uniformly calibrated solvability tests.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The desired region is the set of vectors compatible with estimated pre-panel geometry and a bounded violation budget.

method_exemplars.technique: Propagate a confidence region for the pre-period loading projector jointly with the post-loading drift budget rather than plugging in one estimated subspace.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Honest coverage must separate sampling uncertainty in baseline loading geometry from substantive post-period drift.

literature_map:
He, Li, Shi, and Miao (2026, arXiv:2411.01249v2) formulate direct and spillover effects as sparse outliers after fixed-factor adjustment, but use a majority-valid-controls condition and selection-based asymptotic inference.
Their theory does not give globally honest confidence sets for the full labeled effect vector or a margin-indexed minimax diameter frontier.
Wei (2026, arXiv:2608.13466) gives donor-classification-free sharp partial identification and candidatewise inference under fit-scaled envelopes, while leaving simultaneous effect vectors undeveloped.
Cao and Dowd (2026 revision, arXiv:1902.07343) estimate direct and spillover effects under specified spillover structure, unlike unknown-support sparse decoding.
Sakaguchi and Tagawa (2026 revision, arXiv:2408.00291) impose a spatial autoregressive spillover model and use Bayesian horseshoe inference rather than union-wide frequentist honesty.
Di Stefano and Mellace (2024, arXiv:2403.17624) allow potentially affected donors but do not derive a sharp full-vector adaptation frontier.
Athey et al. (2021, JASA, arXiv:1710.10251) and Agarwal et al. (2021, JASA, arXiv:1902.10920) provide low-rank panel-completion or PCR guarantees primarily for counterfactual prediction.
Ferman and Pinto (2021, Quantitative Economics, DOI:10.3982/QE1596) explain how imperfect fit and unstable factor projections produce post-treatment bias.
Chandrasekaran et al. (2011, SIAM Journal on Optimization, arXiv:0906.2220) establish geometric rank-sparsity incoherence and exact recovery, but not causal honest-inference frontiers.
Nickl and van de Geer (2013, Annals of Statistics, arXiv:1209.1508) connect honest sparse-vector adaptation to composite testing and separation boundaries.
Zhou, Li, and Zhou (2021, JASA, arXiv:1902.00535) construct globally honest sets for the fitted mean X beta while explicitly distinguishing that target from beta itself.
Naumov, Spokoiny, and Ulyanov (2017, arXiv:1703.00871) provide finite-sample bootstrap confidence sets for spectral projectors, but under an i.i.d. centered covariance model.
Zhu (2019, arXiv:1910.10382) shows a sharp validity-efficiency conflict under unknown weak factors, indicating another nonregular boundary if rank is later allowed to vary.
Rambachan and Roth (2023, Review of Economic Studies, DOI:10.1093/restud/rdad018) show that bounded violations of extrapolation assumptions can support sharp partial identification and uniform sensitivity inference.
The scan found no paper combining estimated fixed-factor geometry, unknown sparse attributable effects without beta-min, global full-vector honesty, and matching margin-indexed oracle/adaptive diameter bounds.
